review_candidates.description: Location: Denver, Colorado Compensation: Competitive base salary + package Environment: Smallsat Design and Manufacturing The opportunity Imagine arriving at work knowing the systems you're responsible for aren't supporting another ordinary corporate office. They're supporting a team building spacecraft. EVONA is partnering with a fast-growing international space technology company that is expanding its US operations in Denver and building the infrastructure, engineering capability and teams required to support its next phase of growth. At the centre of that expansion sits IT. As Senior IT Systems Administrator, you'll become the primary IT resource for the US operation — responsible for keeping its people connected, its infrastructure reliable, its cloud environments secure and its systems compliant with the demanding requirements of the US government and defence ecosystem. This isn't a role where you'll spend your day forwarding tickets to somebody else. You'll own things. What will you actually be responsible for? Your environment will span everything from the laptop sitting on an engineer's desk to government-regulated cloud infrastructure. You'll support employees when technology gets in their way, troubleshoot hardware and software issues and manage the workstations, servers, networks and devices that keep the Denver operation running. But that's only the beginning. You'll administer Microsoft GCC High across Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, Intune and Entra ID, alongside Azure Government infrastructure and AWS GovCloud environments. Identity and access will sit firmly within your world. You'll manage onboarding and offboarding, user provisioning, MFA, role-based access, privileged accounts and permissions across both local and cloud environments. You'll also have significant responsibility for cybersecurity. That means monitoring endpoints and infrastructure, investigating suspicious activity, responding to security incidents, managing vulnerabilities, maintaining patching and system-hardening programmes and continuously improving the controls protecting the organisation. When something doesn't look right, you'll investigate it. When something could be more secure, you'll improve it. And when the organisation grows, you'll help make sure the technology and security architecture can grow with it. Security isn't an afterthought here The company operates within an environment where government and defence customers expect considerably more than a password policy and antivirus software. You'll help maintain and strengthen compliance with frameworks and requirements such as: CMMC | NIST 800-171 | FedRAMP | ITAR | DFARS You'll maintain security documentation, inventories, audit evidence, access reviews, logs and control records and help ensure the organisation is ready when customers or auditors need evidence that controls are actually being followed. You'll also evaluate encryption technologies and protocols including AES, RSA, ECC and TLS/SSL, considering how they're applied to data at rest and in transit. That includes disk encryption, certificate handling and key management in environments aligned with FIPS 140-2/140-3 requirements. You'll support backups, restoration testing, disaster recovery and business continuity exercises too. Because in this environment, resilience matters just as much as security. You'll have a lot of technology to play with Depending on the environment, you'll be working across technologies including: Microsoft GCC High Azure Government AWS GovCloud Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory Microsoft Intune Microsoft Defender Microsoft Sentinel / Security Center Windows Server EDR and endpoint security Firewalls, VPNs and networking Identity and privileged access management Vulnerability and patch management Monitoring and logging platforms Encryption and key management You'll also manage and troubleshoot the physical infrastructure behind the operation — switches, routers, storage, wireless networks, firewalls, internet connectivity and office IT equipment. So if you're someone who enjoys being genuinely hands-on rather than specialising in one tiny corner of an enterprise IT department, you'll have plenty to get involved with. Who are we looking for? We're looking for someone with at least five years of experience across systems administration, infrastructure engineering, IT operations, cybersecurity or a closely related field. You'll ideally have a degree in IT, Computer Science or Cybersecurity, although equivalent practical experience is equally interesting. You'll need strong experience within Windows-based enterprise environments and Microsoft 365. Experience with Microsoft GCC High, Azure Government and AWS GovCloud would be particularly valuable because these environments will form an important part of your responsibility. Experience supporting organisations working within CMMC, NIST 800-171, FedRAMP, ITAR, DFARS or similar regulated environments would be highly advantageous. But technical knowledge alone isn't enough. You'll be the person people turn to when something isn't working. So we're looking for someone who can troubleshoot calmly, communicate clearly, document properly and explain technical problems to people who don't necessarily speak IT. Why apply? Because this is an opportunity to join while the US operation is still being built. Rather than inheriting an enormous corporate environment where everything was designed ten years ago and changing anything requires six committees, you'll have the opportunity to influence how infrastructure, security and IT operations develop as the organisation grows. You'll work alongside engineers and technical teams developing next-generation space technology, while collaborating with colleagues across the company's international offices. You'll have autonomy, direct access to leadership and the opportunity to recommend better technology, architecture, processes and security controls when you see an opportunity to improve something. There will also be opportunities for occasional international travel and collaboration with the company's European teams. What’s on offer? Salary: $100,000 – $130,000 USD The final salary will depend on experience and technical background. You'll Also Receive Health insurance coverage Matching 401(k) plan Generous team performance-based bonus Autonomy and direct access to leadership Travel and conference opportunities International collaboration Ongoing learning and career development One final thought Plenty of companies need someone to administer Microsoft 365, manage their network and keep their cloud infrastructure running. Far fewer can offer you the opportunity to do it while helping build the US technology infrastructure behind an international spacecraft company. If you like the idea of owning an environment rather than simply maintaining one — and you want your next IT challenge to involve space, government technology and serious cybersecurity — we'd love to hear from you.

As a Network & Security Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, managing, monitoring, and securing Octane’s network infrastructure while ensuring high availability, performance, and protection against security threats. This role combines hands-on network administration with cybersecurity responsibilities . You will work closely with IT and other teams to maintain secure connectivity, identify and mitigate vulnerabilities, troubleshoot network and security incidents, and continuously improve Octane’s overall infrastructure security. What You'll Be Doing Design, configure, maintain, and monitor network infrastructure, including LAN, WAN, VPNs, firewalls, switches, and routers. Monitor network performance, availability, traffic, and capacity to ensure reliable connectivity. Configure and maintain firewalls, VPNs, network access controls, and security policies. Identify, investigate, and resolve network and security incidents in a timely manner. Monitor security alerts, logs, and network activity to detect potential threats or vulnerabilities. Implement and maintain network security controls, access policies, and segmentation. Conduct regular vulnerability assessments and support remediation of identified security risks. Manage network access, user permissions, and secure remote connectivity. Ensure systems and network devices are properly patched, updated, and securely configured. Support endpoint and infrastructure security initiatives in collaboration with the IT team. Perform troubleshooting and root-cause analysis for recurring network and security issues. Support IT audits, security assessments, and compliance requirements when needed. Evaluate and recommend network and security tools, technologies, and improvements. Contribute to business continuity, disaster recovery, and network resilience initiatives. Key Areas of Ownership Network Infrastructure & Administration Network Security & Firewall Management Cybersecurity Monitoring & Threat Detection VPN & Secure Remote Access Vulnerability Management & Risk Mitigation Network Performance & Availability Incident Response & Troubleshooting Access Control & Security Policies Infrastructure Documentation & Compliance Network & Security Optimization What We're Looking For Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, or a related field. 3–5 years of hands-on experience in network engineering, network security, or infrastructure security. Hands-on experience with firewalls, VPNs, routers, switches, and network security solutions. Strong understanding of network security principles, access controls, segmentation, and secure network architecture. Experience with network monitoring and security monitoring tools. Knowledge of vulnerability management, security hardening, patch management, and risk mitigation. Experience troubleshooting complex network and security incidents. Familiarity with Windows Server, Active Directory, and Microsoft 365 environments is a plus. Knowledge of endpoint security, IDS/IPS, SIEM, or EDR solutions is a plus. Relevant certifications such as CCNA, CCNP, CompTIA Security+, or similar are a plus. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Ability to investigate issues, identify root causes, and implement effective solutions. Strong communication and documentation skills. Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams. Proactive mindset with a strong focus on security, reliability, and continuous improvement. If you’re excited to join a fast-growing company and help build a secure, reliable technology environment, we’d love to hear from you. Send us your updated resume to hr@octane-tech.io with the subject line "Network & Security Engineer" .
